summary.headline: Corona Remedies Q1 FY27 revenue rose 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with EBITDA margin up ~190 bps to 22%.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 21.9% YoY to INR422 crore, with India business up 22.7% against IPM growth of 11.6%, and organic growth of 21.4%. EBITDA rose 33.5% to INR93 crore and PAT rose 30.1% to INR60 crore, with PAT margin at 14.2%. Management kept FY27 guidance of 15% organic revenue growth and 20% PAT growth, but flagged raw material and geopolitical cost risk and said it is premature to extrapolate the Q1 margin. The Europe-GMP hormonal facility was capitalised on 30 June 2026 and export filings are targeted for FY28-29.

financial_highlights.change: +21.9% YoY (vs INR347 crore in Q1 FY26)
+33.5% YoY; margin up ~190 bps (from INR70 crore)
vs INR10 crore in Q1 FY26; mainly amortisation of Wokadine and Bayer brands

segments.name: India business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 97% of revenue and grew 22.7% YoY, roughly twice the IPM growth of 11.6%.

segments.name: International business
segments.commentary: Contributed about 3% of revenue and did not grow in Q1; management says it will stay in the low-single-digit share for the next few years.

segments.name: Therapy areas (PharmaTrac, per management)
segments.commentary: Women's Healthcare grew about 23.3% vs IPM 9.4%; Urology grew 27.6% vs IPM 14.9%; Cardio-metabolic and Pain Management outperformed IPM by 1.7x and 1.4x respectively.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: 15% organic revenue growth plus about 1.5-2% inorganic growth, for about 17% total revenue growth and 20% PAT growth.
Management says it aims to maintain margins 'within a similar range' but will not commit to sustaining Q1 levels given cost volatility.

Raw material: about 70-90 days of stock held at quarter end; new stocks began arriving in June 2026. Management sees possible 100 bps margin hit in coming quarters and is offsetting via other cost cuts.
Hormonal facility asset turnover expected below 1x in FY27, rising to 2-3x over about three years; depreciation on the INR130 crore capex is about INR6.5 crore a year.
Export ramp: dossiers ready by Nov-Dec 2026, then 12-18 months for registration; international launch targeted FY28-29.
Medical representative additions guided at 6-8% per year (about 200-250 MRs), with no MR additions planned in FY27 after about 400 were added in Q4 FY26.
capex_capacity: Europe-GMP hormonal (women's healthcare) facility commercialised on 30 June 2026, after INR130 crore capex; it handles tablets, soft gelatin capsules, ointments and gels.
Ahmedabad oral solid dosage facility Europe-GMP certification renewed.
Manufacturing mix is about 60% in-house and 40% outsourced, expected to stay similar through FY27.
API sourcing: about 60-65% of API needs are met by La Chandra Pharma Lab, in which the company holds a 31% stake (via Remedies Private Limited). La Chandra has EU GMP and a recent US DMF approval.
Hormonal plant to serve the domestic market initially; international dossier filings are in preparation.
demand_pricing: MAT June 2026 PharmaTrac split: volume growth 6.3% vs IPM 1.3%; price-led growth about 8.7% vs IPM 5.6%; new product contribution 3.4% vs IPM 2.9%.
Management says the Q1 India growth split is broadly in line with the MAT split.
Company ranks 26th in IPM (up from 29th a year ago). It is 5th in Women's Healthcare and Pain Management, 9th in Urology, and 20th in Cardio-diabeto (top 10 in new consolidated business).
Two brands now exceed INR100 crore annual revenue (one in MAT June 2023), and more than 40 brands exceed INR10 crore (from 32). Two new INR10 crore entrants are both organic.
Management expects IPM growth of about 9-11%, sustained since December 2025.
Semaglutide: management expects a INR1,500-1,800 crore market and targets a top-10 position, but says focus remains on engine brands.

qa_highlights.question: Is there scope for margin expansion if 20% growth continues, or will incremental growth be reinvested?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited favourable mix and operating leverage in Q1 but would not extrapolate. It said it aims to keep margins in a similar range and cited Southeast Asia and geopolitical cost risk.

qa_highlights.question: Did raw material inflation affect Q1, and will Q2 see more of it?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was largely unaffected due to 70-90 days of inventory. Management sees a possible 100 bps hit and is trying to offset it with other cost reductions to keep the 20% PAT guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the acquired Bayer-Zydus molecule (Dr. Reddy's-sourced, per the analyst) seem to decline YoY, and what is the path to 25% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: External revenue was INR28-30 crore, plus INR20 crore internal. Management called Q1 the launch quarter and said supply-chain integration took priority; it is targeting INR20-40 crore over the coming years.

qa_highlights.question: Split of Q1 growth by volume, price and new launches, and IVF traction?
qa_highlights.answer: Split is in line with MAT: volume 6.3%, price 8.7%, new launches 3.4%. The IVF task force started in April 2026; management says it is too early to comment and will update in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the employee and other expense ratios vs peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is high because about 1,000 MRs (35% of the 3,111 total) were added in three years and productivity per MR is lower; operating leverage should bring it down. Other expenses are mainly UCPMP-governed promotion costs, which are variable.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and amortisation impact from the Wokadine and Bayer acquisitions, and from the hormonal plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Wokadine (INR97 crore plus GST) and Bayer (INR7 crore) are amortised over 10 years. The hormonal plant is depreciated over 20 years (about INR6.5 crore a year).

risks_watch: Raw material and geopolitical (Southeast Asia) cost pressure could cut gross margin by about 100 bps in coming quarters.
Hormonal facility under-recoveries until asset turnover rises from below 1x in FY27 toward 2-3x.
International revenue was flat in Q1; export ramp depends on dossier approvals (FY28-29).
Wokadine and Bayer-Zydus brand ramp is early; management guides to 25% inorganic growth over 2-3 years.
Dependence on La Chandra for about 60-65% of API needs.
Next quarter: whether margin holds near 22% EBITDA and the India growth rate stays about twice the IPM.
key_quotes: At this stage, it would be premature to comment on the sustainability of current levels, although our endeavor is to maintain margins within a similar range.

While we are encouraged by this performance, we remain cautious about extrapolating the current margin profile into coming quarters given the evolving cost environment due to geopolitical Southeast Asia risk.
We continue to target 15% revenue growth and 20% PAT growth over the FY27.
So, first quarter can't be considered for the future coming quarters numbers perspective, but we are eyeing what we have committed of our 25% growth
summary.management_tone: Confident on the India growth story, volume and brand momentum, and the FY27 guidance, which was kept unchanged. Noticeably cautious on margins: management declined to extrapolate Q1 profitability, citing geopolitical and Southeast Asia cost volatility, and was evasive on the Bayer-Zydus molecule's YoY decline, attributing it to launch and supply-chain integration.

adds.what: Europe-GMP hormonal (women's healthcare) facility after INR130 crore capex; tablets, soft gelatin capsules, ointments and gels

growth.why: FY27 guidance held at 15% organic plus 1.5-2% inorganic (about 17% total) and 20% PAT growth; backing is Q1 volume growth of 6.3% vs IPM 1.3%, new brands and the commissioned INR130 crore hormonal plant, but no concrete order or capacity-utilisation numbers tie the guidance to the plant, which is expected to run below 1x asset turnover in FY27.
